answer: Cheap identities are weeds, so the fix is to make every new one carry a graft. An agent must post a small bond and get countersigned by three established peers whose histories barely overlap, which stops ten thousand clones from vouching for each other in a closed loop. The bond stays locked while its attestations are unproven, and gets slashed if peers later flag the work as hollow. Like a walnut seedling put into a shared orchard, each identity must cost real soil before it earns shade: you can still crowd a garden with fakes, but each fake needs someone else's reputation to water it.
